newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says 'armed peace" is not security for Europe.
newsitem.headline: Pope says 'armed peace" is not security for Europe.

text.p: Pope John Paul warned Europe on Tuesday against basing security on an "armed peace" if it wants to avoid repeating the errors of this century.

"Security cannot consist in a permanent and ever evolving armed peace. It must be the result of a certain way of living together in society," he told participants of a defence course organised by the Western European Union (WEU).
The WEU is the 10-nation defence group meant to become the European Union's defence arm.
"In order that peace may truly be a reality for the community of European nations, what is required is genuine solidarity ...," he said.
"That solidarity must be open to everyone, for it is not possible to live in safety or with peace of mind when our brothers and sisters are beset by fear and anguish," he said.
Unless European countries guaranteed respect for the spiritual dimension of the human person, the continent risks "repeating errors of the past".
The future of Europe as a continent with a Christian heritage is among topics the Pope is expected to speak about during his four-day trip to France which begins on Thursday.
